title: Managing product delivery: purpose, objectives and four activities
blurb: Explain how managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and team managers, and name its four activities and products.
question: A team manager agrees a work package with the project manager, builds the products and sends weekly progress reports. Which process is the team manager using, and what is its purpose?

teach.h: The team manager's side of the handshake
teach.body: Formally: managing product delivery exists to control the link between the project manager and the team manager, by agreeing what is needed for the acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products. In plain English: it is how a team takes on a piece of work from the PM, builds it, reports on it and hands it back, under clear agreed terms.

teach.h: Objectives: managing product delivery makes sure that...
items: Work on the products allocated to the team is authorized and agreed.
Team managers and their teams are clear about what is to be produced and the expected effort, cost and timescales.
The planned products are delivered to quality expectations and within tolerance.
Accurate progress information is given to the project manager at an agreed frequency.

teach.caption: All four are carried out by the team manager. Where there is no separate team manager, the PM may take on the role.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a rail signalling upgrade
teach.body: Brightwell Rail hires an outside contractor to rewire signals for its station upgrade. The contractor's team manager, Owen Price, does not use PRINCE2, but he accepts a work package from project manager Sofia Marques, draws up a team plan and sends weekly checkpoint reports. When senior user Dev Patel calls Owen to ask for an extra signal, Owen refers him to Sofia: in managing product delivery, the team takes direction from the PM, not straight from the board.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) The project board is NOT involved in managing product delivery. (2) A team manager reports new issues, risks and lessons to the PM and acts on the PM's instructions, never the board's directly. (3) Checkpoint reports go TM to PM; highlight reports go PM to board. (4) Suppliers do not need to use PRINCE2 to work this way.

items: Purpose: control the link between project manager and team manager.
Four activities: accept, execute and evaluate a work package, then notify completion.
The team manager produces checkpoint reports and may develop a team plan.
PM accountable for execute a work package; project support informed of completion.
The board is not involved; suppliers need not use PRINCE2.

summary: You can now explain the purpose and objectives of managing product delivery, name its four activities and say how it hands work to and from controlling a stage. You can also place checkpoint reports and team plans correctly.

A.q: Which is the purpose of the managing product delivery process?
options: Assign work and keep the stage within tolerance
Let the board be accountable through key decisions
Control the link between the PM and the team manager
Give the board what it needs to review the stage
A.why: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the team manager by agreeing requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery (manual 17.1).

whyNot.0: That is the purpose of controlling a stage.
whyNot.1: That is the purpose of directing a project.
whyNot.3: That is the purpose of managing a stage boundary.

A.q: Which report does a team manager use to tell the project manager how a work package is progressing?
options: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
End stage report
Exception report
A.why: The team manager reports work package status to the PM through checkpoint reports at the frequency agreed in the work package.

whyNot.1: Highlight reports go from the PM to the project board.
whyNot.2: End stage reports go from the PM to the board at a stage boundary.
whyNot.3: Exception reports go from the PM to the board when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.

A.q: Which managing product delivery activity is used when the team manager and project manager agree what will be delivered and how it will be reported?
options: Execute a work package
Accept a work package
Evaluate a work package
Notify work package completion
A.why: In accept a work package the PM and TM agree what is to be delivered, reporting requirements, constraints and procedures, and the TM agrees to deliver it (manual 17.4.1).

whyNot.0: Execute a work package builds the products to the agreed requirements.
whyNot.2: Evaluate a work package reports results back to the PM.
whyNot.3: Notify work package completion hands the finished work back.

B.q:
Which two statements about managing product delivery are correct?
1. The project board is not involved in this process.
2. Suppliers must use PRINCE2 to take part in this process.
3. Team managers report new risks directly to the project board.
4. Accurate progress information is given to the PM at an agreed frequency.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: The board is not involved in managing product delivery (1), and one objective is accurate progress information to the PM at an agreed frequency (4) (manual 17.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: suppliers need not use PRINCE2.
whyNot.2: Both are false: suppliers need not use PRINCE2, and new risks go to the PM.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is false: team managers notify the PM, who decides whether to escalate.

B.q: A board member asks a team manager directly to add a feature to a product being built. How should the team manager respond?
options: Add it within the work package tolerance
Raise an exception report to the board
Record it in the team plan and proceed
Refer the request to the project manager
B.why: In execute a work package the TM notifies the PM of new issues and takes any action required by the PM, not by the board directly (manual 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Work package tolerance covers deviations in agreed work, not new requests from the board.
whyNot.1: Exception reports are raised by the PM to the board, not by team managers.
whyNot.2: The team plan is not the place to accept a new requirement without the PM.

B.q: Which role is accountable for the execute a work package activity?
options: The project manager
The team manager
The executive
Project assurance
B.why: The official RACI for execute a work package makes the PM accountable; project assurance is consulted (manual tab 17.2).

whyNot.1: The team manager carries out the work but is not the accountable role in the official RACI.
whyNot.2: The executive is not involved in execute a work package.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted, not accountable.

C.q: Which process produces checkpoint reports, and which process reviews them?
options: Controlling a stage produces; directing a project reviews
Managing product delivery produces; directing a project reviews
Managing product delivery produces; controlling a stage reviews
Controlling a stage produces; managing product delivery reviews
C.why: Team managers produce checkpoint reports in managing product delivery; the PM reviews them in controlling a stage (evaluate work package status).

whyNot.0: The PM produces highlight reports in controlling a stage, not checkpoint reports.
whyNot.1: The board does not review checkpoint reports; they go to the PM.
whyNot.3: This reverses the direction: checkpoint reports flow from the team to the PM.

C.q: When a work package is finished, which activity is used, and which role is informed?
options: Evaluate a work package; the senior user
Notify work package completion; the business layer
Execute a work package; the senior supplier
Notify work package completion; project support
C.why: Completion is notified to the PM in notify work package completion, and project support is informed (manual 17.4.4, tab 17.2).

whyNot.0: The senior user is not informed of work package completion.
whyNot.1: The business layer is not informed of work package completion.
whyNot.2: Execute a work package is the building activity, and the senior supplier is not informed of completion.

C.q: During execute a work package, a team completes a quality review on a product. What should the team manager do?
options: Approve the product on behalf of the board
Update the quality register and tell the PM
Report the result in a highlight report
Close the matching entry in the issue register
C.why: The TM notifies the PM of completed quality activities and updates the quality register (manual 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Approval is given by the authority named in the product description, not by the TM on the board's behalf.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports are the PM's reports to the board.
whyNot.3: A quality review result is recorded in the quality register, not by closing an issue.

reteach.title: A kitchen fitter working for a builder
reteach.question: A builder hires a specialist kitchen fitter. How do they keep the job under control without the homeowner phoning the fitter every day?

blocks.body: The fitter agrees the job sheet with the builder, fits the kitchen, sends the builder a short progress note each week and tells the builder when it is done. If the homeowner wants an extra cupboard, the fitter sends them to the builder. Builder = project manager, fitter = team manager, homeowner = board. That is managing product delivery.

blocks.text: The homeowner (board) does not instruct the fitter (team manager) directly. Requests go through the builder (PM).

explain.body: Managing product delivery agrees the requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of the specialist products between the PM and the TM.

test.q: What does managing product delivery agree between the PM and the team manager?
options: Terms for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery
Stage tolerances and the plan for the next stage
The benefits and post-project review arrangements
The project approach and the contents of the project brief
test.why: The purpose of managing product delivery is achieved by agreeing requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products (manual 17.1).

whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the board, and the next stage plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.2: Benefits reviews are planned in the benefits management approach, not agreed with team managers.
whyNot.3: The project approach and brief are produced in starting up a project.

explain.body: Before work is allocated, the PM and TM agree what will be delivered, reporting, constraints and procedures, and whether it is achievable. The TM then agrees to deliver it and may produce a team plan.

test.q: In accept a work package, what does the team manager check before agreeing to deliver?
options: That the business case is still viable
That the stage tolerances are correct
That the requirements can be achieved
That the project board has approved it
test.why: Accept a work package covers whether the work package requirements are reasonable and can be achieved (manual 17.4.1).

whyNot.0: Business case viability is reviewed by the PM and board, not checked by the TM here.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are the board's concern; the TM works within work package tolerances.
whyNot.3: The board is not involved in managing product delivery; the PM authorizes the work package.

explain.body: The TM manages the building of the products to the work package requirements, notifies the PM of new issues, risks or lessons, updates the quality register and reports status.

test.q: A team member identifies a new risk during the work. Who should the team manager notify?
options: The project board
The executive
Project assurance
The project manager
test.why: In execute a work package the TM notifies the PM of any new issues, risks or lessons (manual 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: The board is not involved in managing product delivery; only the PM escalates to the board.
whyNot.1: The executive is not involved in execute a work package.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is consulted on the activity but does not receive the team's risks.

explain.body: Evaluate a work package reports the results back to the PM so progress is visible. Notify work package completion returns the finished work, just as it was accepted.

test.q: What is the aim of the notify work package completion activity?
options: To ask the board to accept the products
To close the project's quality register
To return the finished work to the PM
To start the next stage of the project
test.why: Just as the work package was accepted from the PM, its completion is notified back to the PM (manual 17.4.4).

whyNot.0: The board is not involved in managing product delivery.
whyNot.1: The quality register is closed in closing a project.
whyNot.3: The next stage is authorized by the board after a stage boundary.
